items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: when I first, when I went to California with Louis Prima in 1937

ctx.x: Never. Never did sit in with a colored musician. Oddly enough, when I first, when I went to California with Louis Prima in 1937, we had a piano player, I don't remember his name, but he was a great piano, relief piano player. And we'd get on the stand to play while he was, and Louis would say, keep on playing. He said, you and Louis, because Frank Venera wasn't the greatest pianist in the world for jazz. And Louis would let him play with us and get the band on and say, believe me, that was the first colored…
Well, I can remember that, sure, up into the 60s or so, not a problem with anybody who tried to do that. Well, the funniest thing

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: I first went to California. July the 17th, 1937. Uh huh. With Louis Prima. Louis Prima's band.

ctx.x: I wanted to, if you're through with that, I wanted to ask you a question. Yeah. When did you first go to New York?

When did I first go to New York? Uh huh. I first went to California. Oh. Where was that? I first went to California. July the 17th, 1937. Uh huh. With Louis Prima. Louis Prima's band. And 1937, July 37. I went there with an ulterior motive. I don't think I ever told Louis about this, but it was an ulterior motive in the back of my mind. I had a lot of people that I had for, that I, if I was out there for six months, I could get to be a full member in the union. And I had a man by the name of Lou Forbes, who was…
Who did you first record with?
